payload.instruction: Put a frog in the toilet
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Is a frog visibly present inside the toilet bowl?
node.criteria: Pass if the image clearly shows a frog within the toilet bowl; fail if the bowl is visible and no frog is inside it; unknown if the bowl or its contents cannot be assessed reliably.
node.binding: Assess the frog’s placement relative to the toilet bowl in the image, using the toilet in the input image as the reference. A frog elsewhere does not satisfy this check.

node_traces.evidence: A frog is clearly visible inside the toilet bowl in the edited image.

fulfillment: The binding is underspecified (`visibly (...)`) and the node’s completion criterion is too permissive: it treats one frog inside the bowl as complete, while the edited image shows additional frogs on the lid/tank and floor, so the requested edit has progressed but is not cleanly limited to the bowl. Make the binding explicitly distinguish the requested frog-in-bowl placement from other visible frogs, and ensure the criterion evaluates the whole edit against the instruction: count clear in-bowl placement as progress, but do not equate that alone with complete fulfillment when the image also contains apparent misplaced additions. Preserve an unknown outcome when placement or image evidence is genuinely ambiguous. The support traces are valid and queried, with no transport/schema/dependency failure; their repeated high-confidence claims are not independent confirmation and appear to have collapsed the decision to a single presence check. Require evidence tied to the edited image’s relevant locations and report partial progress rather than completion when the full requested change is not satisfied.
s2: The support node should remain an evidence/visibility check, not decide fulfillment or impose a “cleanly limited to the bowl” requirement absent from the instruction. Its current criterion and binding focus on whether a frog is inside the bowl, so the pass is valid evidence of progress; the downstream yes appears to result from treating that single observation as sufficient for completion. Make the node report location-specific evidence across the edited image—here, frogs are visible in the bowl, on the raised lid, and on the floor—and keep its pass/fail/unknown semantics limited to whether those regions can be assessed. Ensure the downstream fulfillment decision compares all observed changes with the actual request and rubric: the in-bowl frog is progress, while the extra frogs are unrelated additions, not grounds to invent a requirement that no other frogs appear. Preserve unknown for genuinely unclear placement. Traces are valid and queried, with no transport, schema, or dependency failure; repeated high confidence in the same presence claim is not independent confirmation.
